title: C5 factorization-depth sweep at fixed per-factor beam ratio
question: At approximately fixed B/F=0.625, does increasing product-key factorization depth from two through five factors change target retention and reduce the fraction of states subjected to reranking?
hypothesis: At a fixed per-factor beam ratio B/F, proposal coverage and capability retention should be approximately depth-invariant while states_scored_over_M should decrease approximately as (B/F)^d. Deeper factorization may deviate from this because narrower factor slices can change the learned product-key geometry.

arms.name: d2_f8_b5
arms.intervention: two-factor product-key addressing with factor size 8 and beam 5

arms.name: d3_f8_b5
arms.intervention: three-factor product-key addressing with factor size 8 and beam 5

arms.name: d4_f8_b5
arms.intervention: four-factor product-key addressing with factor size 8 and beam 5

arms.name: d5_f8_b5
arms.intervention: five-factor product-key addressing with factor size 8 and beam 5

endpoints.name: target_recall_retention_ratio
endpoints.description: selective target recall divided by exhaustive target recall

decision_rule.condition: For every registered depth d in {2,3,4,5} and every M in {128,256,512}, report exhaustive target recall, selective target recall, target-recall retention, proposal retention, states scored/M, absolute scored count, pair-generation operations, arithmetic, and occupancy with exact pooled counts.
decision_rule.licenses: a workload-specific factorization-depth measurement at fixed B/F on the registered C5 construction.
decision_rule.does_not_license: universal optimal factor count, semantic retrieval guarantees, asymptotic sublinear scaling, or hardware speedup.

decision_rule.condition: A depth arm satisfies the registered capability floor only when target_recall_retention_ratio is at least 0.90 at every M.
decision_rule.licenses: that the specific fixed-depth arm meets the registered capability floor on the tested workload.
decision_rule.does_not_license: that the depth is generally optimal.

decision_rule.condition: Compare observed states_scored_over_M with the fixed-ratio geometric reference (5/8)^d and report the deviation for every depth.
decision_rule.licenses: evidence about whether the reranking fraction follows the expected product-cell fraction at fixed B/F.

held_constant: 48 fixed training codes versus 16 held-out target codes
same task stream and pooled count aggregation
protocol_note: Mechanism experiment only. The depth sweep is evaluated through the same generalized multi-factor product-key implementation for all four depths. The registered geometric reference predicts scored fractions of 39.06%, 24.41%, 15.26%, and 9.54% for d=2,3,4,5 respectively. These are expectations, not decision thresholds.
